callouts.label: Notice a Change
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents notice a change.
callouts.description: Pay attention to changes in mood, behavior, connection, sleep, or functioning.
callouts.tip: One sign does not prove a diagnosis. Take concerning patterns seriously.

callouts.label: Choose Time and Place
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents choose time and place.
callouts.description: A private, calm moment can make conversation easier.
callouts.tip: Do not wait for a perfect script. Safety takes priority over privacy.

callouts.label: Listen
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents listen.
callouts.description: Give attention without rushing to fix, debate, or compare.
callouts.tip: Reflect what you hear. Let pauses happen.

callouts.label: Ask Directly About Safety
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents ask directly about safety.
callouts.description: If you are worried about suicide or self-harm, ask clearly and calmly.
callouts.tip: Asking does not plant the idea. A yes, maybe, or unclear answer needs adult and professional help.

callouts.label: Validate
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents validate.
callouts.description: Acknowledge that the person’s feelings and experience matter.
callouts.tip: Validation is not agreement with every conclusion. Avoid minimizing or promising a quick fix.

callouts.label: Connect a Trusted Adult
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents connect a trusted adult.
callouts.description: Bring in a safe adult who can help assess and act.
callouts.tip: Do not promise secrecy about serious safety concerns. Keep reaching out until someone responds.

callouts.label: Connect Professional Help
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents connect professional help.
callouts.description: Counselors, clinicians, and crisis professionals can assess risk and provide care.
callouts.tip: Offer to help make contact. Treatment may involve several kinds of support.

callouts.label: Respond to Urgent Crisis
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents respond to urgent crisis.
callouts.description: Immediate danger requires emergency or crisis help now.
callouts.tip: Stay nearby when safe and reduce access to immediate danger with adult help. Follow local emergency guidance.

callouts.label: Keep Boundaries
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents keep boundaries.
callouts.description: A caring friend is not a therapist or sole safety plan.
callouts.tip: Share responsibility with adults and professionals. It is okay to rest and say what you can do.

callouts.label: Follow Up
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents follow up.
callouts.description: A later message or conversation shows that care continues.
callouts.tip: Ask how the support plan is working. Recovery is rarely one conversation.

callouts.label: Care for Yourself
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents care for yourself.
callouts.description: Supporting someone can be emotionally demanding.
callouts.tip: Talk with a trusted adult or counselor. Your wellbeing matters too.

callouts.label: Build a Support Team
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents build a support team.
callouts.description: Several caring people and services create a stronger safety net.
callouts.tip: The person should be included in planning when possible. Shared support reduces isolation.
